title: The Open Hand
summary: A plain-language lesson about consent, refusal, and purpose-specific permission in Calypso’s Promise.
learningObjectives: Explain that permission should be specific to a purpose.
Recognize that refusal should not cause punishment or loss of core access.
Distinguish reviewing a permission from granting it.
body: The Law of the Open Hand means that a choice is only meaningful when the purpose is clear and refusal remains real. A person may inspect a permission, ask questions, decline it, or withdraw it later according to the documented rules. Progress must not depend on granting broader access than the current task requires.
plainLanguageBody: You should be told what a permission is for before choosing. You may say no without losing the core experience. Looking at a permission is not the same as agreeing to it.

claims.text: Purpose-specific permission is a product rule of Calypso’s Promise.
The project prohibits rewarding broader consent merely because it is broader.

comprehensionPrompt: Which action shows a meaningful choice: reviewing a permission and deciding freely, or receiving extra progress only for accepting it?
